title: Cricket Pitch Dimensions & Measurements
answer: A standard cricket pitch is a rectangular area measuring exactly 22 yards (66 feet / 20.12 metres) in length between the bowling creases, and 10 feet (3.05 metres) in width.
highlights: Pitch Length: 22 yards = 66 feet = 20.12 metres (between wickets / bowling creases)
Pitch Width: 10 feet = 3.05 metres
Stumps Height: 28 inches (71.1 cm) above the pitch surface
Bowling Crease Width: 8 feet 8 inches (2.64 metres)

title: International Cricket Formats — Test, ODI & T20I
answer: International cricket is played in three primary formats: Test Cricket (the traditional pinnacle played over 5 days with two innings per side and unlimited overs using a red/pink ball), One Day Internationals (ODIs — 50 overs per side using a white ball), and Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is — 20 overs per side).
highlights: Test Cricket: 5 days duration, 2 innings per side, minimum 90 overs per day, red ball (pink ball in day-night tests)
One Day International (ODI): 50 overs per side, white ball, 10 overs max per bowler, 3 fielding powerplays
Twenty20 (T20I): 20 overs per side, white ball, 4 overs max per bowler, 6 overs powerplay
Governing Body: International Cricket Council (ICC, founded 1909)

title: ICC Men's Cricket World Cup (ODI) Winners (1975 – Present)
answer: Australia is the most successful team in ICC Men's Cricket World Cup history with 6 titles (1987, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2015, 2023). India (1983, 2011) and West Indies (1975, 1979) have won 2 titles each, while Pakistan (1992), Sri Lanka (1996), and England (2019) have won 1 title each.
highlights: India (2 Titles): 1983 (Kapil Dev captain) and 2011 (MS Dhoni captain)
West Indies (2 Titles): 1975, 1979 (Clive Lloyd captain)
Pakistan: 1992 (Imran Khan captain) | Sri Lanka: 1996 (Arjuna Ranatunga captain) | England: 2019 (Eoin Morgan captain)

answer: India and England and the West Indies are the most successful teams in ICC Men's T20 World Cup history with 2 titles each: India (2007 under MS Dhoni, 2024 under Rohit Sharma), West Indies (2012, 2016), England (2010, 2022), Pakistan (2009), Sri Lanka (2014), and Australia (2021).

West Indies: 2012 & 2016 (captain Daren Sammy)
England: 2010 (Paul Collingwood) & 2022 (Jos Buttler)
Pakistan: 2009 | Sri Lanka: 2014 | Australia: 2021

title: FIFA World Cup Champions (Men's) (1930 – Present)
answer: Brazil has won the most FIFA World Cup titles in football history with 5 championships (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002). Germany and Italy have won 4 titles each, Argentina has 3 titles (1978, 1986, 2022), France and Uruguay have 2 each, while England and Spain have 1 each.
highlights: Argentina (3 Titles): 1978, 1986 (Maradona), 2022 (Messi)
France (2 Titles): 1998, 2018 | Uruguay (2 Titles): 1930, 1950 | Spain: 2010 | England: 1966

title: Olympic Motto & Meaning of the Five Olympic Rings
answer: The official Olympic motto is 'Citius, Altius, Fortius – Communiter', which translates from Latin to 'Faster, Higher, Stronger – Together' (the word 'Communiter' was formally added by the IOC in 2021). The five interlocking Olympic rings represent the union of the five inhabited continents (Africa, Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania).
highlights: Motto: Citius, Altius, Fortius – Communiter (Faster, Higher, Stronger – Together)
Ring Colors: Blue, Yellow, Black, Green, Red on a white field (at least one color appears on the flag of every nation on Earth)
Designer: Baron Pierre de Coubertin (1913)
Governing Body: International Olympic Committee (IOC, founded 1894 in Lausanne, Switzerland)

title: Tennis Grand Slam Tournaments — Chronological Order & Surfaces
answer: The four Grand Slam (Major) tennis tournaments in chronological order throughout the calendar year are: 1) Australian Open (January, Hard court, Melbourne); 2) French Open / Roland Garros (May–June, Clay court, Paris); 3) Wimbledon (June–July, Grass court, London); and 4) US Open (August–September, Hard court, New York City).
highlights: 1. Australian Open: Melbourne Park (Plexicushion/GreenSet Hard Court, January)
2. French Open (Roland Garros): Stade Roland Garros, Paris (Red Clay Court, May–June)
3. Wimbledon: All England Club, London (Grass Court, June–July — Oldest tournament, est. 1877)
4. US Open: USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, NYC (Laykold Hard Court, August–September)

title: Badminton Scoring Rules & Court Dimensions
answer: Badminton is played as best of 3 games to 21 points using rally scoring (points are scored on every serve regardless of who served). At 20-20, the side that gains a 2-point lead first wins the game; at 29-29, the side scoring the 30th point wins.
highlights: Scoring System: 21 points per game (Rally point system, best of 3 games)
Deuce Rule: Must win by 2 points up to a maximum cap of 30 points (sudden death at 29-29)
Court Dimensions: Length = 13.40 m (44 ft); Width = 5.18 m (singles) / 6.10 m (doubles)
Net Height: 1.55 m (5 ft 1 in) at posts and 1.524 m (5 ft) at center

title: Football (Soccer) — Match Duration, Pitch Dimensions & Rules
answer: A standard professional football (soccer) match consists of two 45-minute halves (total 90 minutes) plus stoppage/injury time. Each team fields 11 players including 1 goalkeeper. Standard international pitch dimensions are 100–110 metres in length by 64–75 metres in width.
highlights: Match Duration: 90 minutes (two 45-minute halves with a 15-minute half-time interval)
Extra Time: Two 15-minute halves (30 mins total) followed by penalty shootout in knockout ties
Pitch Dimensions: Length 100–110 m (110–120 yd), Width 64–75 m (70–80 yd)
Goal Post Size: 7.32 m (8 yards / 24 ft) wide by 2.44 m (8 ft) high

title: Marathon Distance (42.195 km / 26.219 miles)
answer: The official distance of a standard marathon is exactly 42.195 kilometres (26 miles 385 yards). This standard distance was established during the 1908 Olympic Games in London from Windsor Castle to the White City Stadium Royal Box.
highlights: Exact Distance: 42.195 km (26 miles 385 yards / 26.219 miles)
Historical Origin: Commemorates the run of Greek messenger Pheidippides from the Battle of Marathon to Athens (490 BCE)
Standardization: Standardized by the IAAF (World Athletics) in 1921 based on the 1908 London route

title: Basketball Rules, Court Dimensions & Hoop Height
answer: In basketball, two teams of 5 players compete to score points by throwing the ball through an elevated hoop positioned exactly 10 feet (3.05 metres) above the floor. NBA games consist of four 12-minute quarters (48 minutes total), while FIBA games consist of four 10-minute quarters (40 minutes).
highlights: Hoop Height: Exactly 10 feet (3.05 metres) above the court
Court Dimensions: 94 feet × 50 feet (28.65 m × 15.24 m in NBA) / 28 m × 15 m (FIBA)
Scoring: Free throw = 1 point; Field goal inside arc = 2 points; Beyond arc = 3 points (23 ft 9 in / 7.24 m in NBA)
Shot Clock: 24 seconds to attempt a field goal that touches the rim

title: Field Hockey Rules, Match Duration & Pitch Size
answer: A field hockey match is played between two teams of 11 players (including a goalkeeper) over 60 minutes divided into four 15-minute quarters. The pitch measures 91.4 metres (100 yards) in length by 55.0 metres (60 yards) in width.
highlights: Duration: 60 minutes (4 quarters of 15 minutes each)
Players: 11 players per side on the pitch
Pitch Dimensions: 91.40 m × 55.00 m (100 yd × 60 yd)
Shooting Circle (D-Area): Goals can only be scored from inside the 14.63-metre (16 yd) striking circle (D)

title: Volleyball Rules, Net Height & Court Dimensions
answer: In volleyball, two teams of 6 players are separated by a net. Teams play best of 5 sets: the first 4 sets are played to 25 points (must win by 2), and a deciding 5th set is played to 15 points. Teams are allowed a maximum of 3 touches to return the ball across the net.
highlights: Scoring: First to 25 points with a 2-point lead (5th set to 15 points; rally point scoring)
Court Dimensions: 18 metres × 9 metres (divided into two 9m × 9m halves)
Net Height: 2.43 metres (7 ft 11⅝ in) for Men; 2.24 metres (7 ft 4⅛ in) for Women
Specialist Position: Libero (defensive specialist wearing a contrasting jersey)

title: Table Tennis (Ping Pong) Rules & Regulations
answer: In table tennis, a game is won by the first player or pair to score 11 points with at least a 2-point margin (best of 5 or 7 games). Service alternates every 2 points, and switches on every single point if the score reaches 10-10 (deuce).
highlights: Game Points: 11 points per game (best of 5 or 7 games)
Service Order: Alternates every 2 serves; alternates every 1 serve at 10-10 deuce
Table Dimensions: 2.74 m (9.0 ft) long, 1.525 m (5.0 ft) wide, 76 cm (30.0 in) high
Net Height: 15.25 cm (6.0 inches)

title: Kabaddi Rules, Raid Clock & Team Structure
answer: Kabaddi is an ancient contact sport played between two teams of 7 active players on court. A match lasts 40 minutes (two 20-minute halves). A lone 'raider' enters the opponent's half chanting 'kabaddi' and has a maximum of 30 seconds to tag defenders and return safely without being tackled.
highlights: Players: 7 active players on court per team (plus 5 substitutes)
Match Duration: 40 minutes (two 20-minute halves with a 5-minute half-time)
Raid Clock: Maximum 30 seconds per raid; raider must continuously chant the 'cant'
Special Rules: Do-or-Die Raid (3rd consecutive empty raid requires scoring or raider is out), Super Tackle (tackling raider with 3 or fewer defenders awards 2 points)

title: Chess — Board Setup, Pieces & Rules of the Game
answer: Chess is a two-player strategy board game played on an 8×8 grid of 64 squares. Each player begins with 16 pieces: 1 King, 1 Queen, 2 Rooks, 2 Knights, 2 Bishops, and 8 Pawns. The ultimate objective is to checkmate the opponent's king, putting it under inescapable attack.
highlights: Board Setup: 64 squares (32 light, 32 dark); white square on bottom-right corner
Pieces per Player: 1 King (infinite value), 1 Queen (9 pts), 2 Rooks (5 pts each), 2 Bishops (3 pts each), 2 Knights (3 pts each), 8 Pawns (1 pt each)
Special Moves: Castling (King safety + Rook activation), En Passant (pawn capture), Pawn Promotion (converting pawn on 8th rank to Queen/Rook/Bishop/Knight)
Governing Body: International Chess Federation (FIDE, founded 1924 in Paris)

title: Formula 1 (F1) Championship Points System
answer: In FIA Formula One World Championship Grand Prix races, points are awarded to the top 10 finishers: 1st (25 pts), 2nd (18 pts), 3rd (15 pts), 4th (12 pts), 5th (10 pts), 6th (8 pts), 7th (6 pts), 8th (4 pts), 9th (2 pts), and 10th (1 pt). An extra 1 bonus point is awarded for the fastest lap if the driver finishes in the top 10.
highlights: Grand Prix Points: 1st: 25 | 2nd: 18 | 3rd: 15 | 4th: 12 | 5th: 10 | 6th: 8 | 7th: 6 | 8th: 4 | 9th: 2 | 10th: 1
Fastest Lap: 1 bonus point awarded to the driver with fastest lap if finishing in top 10
Sprint Race Points: Top 8 finishers receive 8-7-6-5-4-3-2-1 points respectively

title: Usain Bolt — 100m & 200m World Sprint Records
answer: Jamaican sprinter Usain Bolt holds the world record for the 100-metre sprint at 9.58 seconds and the 200-metre sprint at 19.19 seconds, both set at the 2009 World Athletics Championships in Berlin, Germany. He is widely acclaimed as the fastest human in history.
highlights: 100m World Record: 9.58 seconds (Set 16 August 2009 in Berlin)
200m World Record: 19.19 seconds (Set 20 August 2009 in Berlin)
Olympic Medals: 8 Olympic Gold Medals (Triple-Triple sprint sweep in 2008, 2012, 2016)
Top Speed Recorded: 44.72 km/h (27.78 mph) between 60m and 80m marks

title: Michael Phelps — Most Decorated Olympian of All Time
answer: Michael Phelps (USA Swimming) is the most successful and most decorated Olympian of all time, with a total of 28 Olympic medals (23 Gold, 3 Silver, 2 Bronze) won across five Olympic Games (2000, 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016).
highlights: Total Olympic Medals: 28 medals (23 Gold, 3 Silver, 2 Bronze)
Beijing 2008 Feat: Won a record 8 Gold Medals in a single Olympic Games, breaking Mark Spitz's 1972 record
Individual Olympic Golds: Record 13 individual Olympic Gold Medals

title: Rohit Sharma's 264 Runs — Highest Individual Score in ODI History
answer: Rohit Sharma holds the world record for the highest individual score in One Day International (ODI) cricket history, scoring 264 runs off 173 balls (with 33 fours and 9 sixes) for India against Sri Lanka at Eden Gardens, Kolkata on 13 November 2014.
highlights: Score: 264 runs off 173 balls (Strike Rate: 152.60)
Boundaries: 33 fours and 9 sixes (World record 186 runs in boundaries alone)
Venue & Date: Eden Gardens, Kolkata (13 November 2014)
Historic Achievement: Rohit Sharma is the only cricketer in history to score three ODI double centuries (209, 264, 208*)
